question_text: Write the parametric equations of the circle 2x² + 2y² = 7.

insider_note: The radius is √(7/2), an awkward surd, and it must be carried as it stands — squaring it away or writing 7/2 as the radius is the only place this question goes wrong.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Divide to the standard form
steps.margin_note: One mark. Divide the whole equation by 2, including the right side.
steps.memory_tip: Standard form x² + y² = r². The right side is r squared.
steps.why: The coefficients of x² and y² must be 1 before the right side can be read as r². Here 7/2 is r², so the radius is its square root.

steps.label: Write the parametric equations
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Keep the surd; a decimal is not an exact answer.
steps.memory_tip: Centre at the origin: x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ.
lines: The centre is the origin, so
x = r cos θ,  y = r sin θ
steps.why: A point on a circle centred at the origin is at distance r in the direction θ, so its coordinates are r cos θ and r sin θ. The surd stays as it is.
common_mistakes: Leaving θ out of the answer.
